articles.title: Microsoft breaks another patch Tuesday record
articles.summary: Engineers at Microsoft typically enjoy a quieter summer to take vacations and spend time with family, as is common at many companies. But this year, the season has been unusually busy for Windows and security engineers, thanks to new AI models that are discovering software vulnerabilities at a rapid pace. Sources tell me that Microsoft will set another patch Tuesday record today, the third in just
articles.body:
Engineers at Microsoft typically enjoy a quieter summer to take vacations and spend time with family, as is common at many companies. But this year, the season has been unusually busy for Windows and security engineers, thanks to new AI models that are discovering software vulnerabilities at a rapid pace. Sources tell me that Microsoft will set another patch Tuesday record today, the third in just a few months.
It all kicked off in April when Anthropic’s new Mythos model found security vulnerabilities in “every major operating system and web browser.” A few weeks later, OpenAI released its own cybersecurity-focused model to trusted partners. Sources familiar with Microsoft’s security work tell me both of these models have contributed to a record-breaking series of patch Tuesdays over the summer period.
Microsoft typically patches around 100 flaws every month, but in June it set a new record of around 200 fixes. July’s patch Tuesday was even bigger, with Microsoft patching at least 570 security holes, almost triple the number of June’s record-breaking release. Microsoft engineers had a chance to catch their breath a bit in August when they plugged nearly 400 security vulnerabilities.
I understand today’s September patch Tuesday is about to set a new record, with more than 650 security fixes for Windows alone. That’s six times the number that usually got patched before the AI models arrived. Engineers have been busy over the summer verifying fixes for hundreds of important patches, which include remote code vulnerabilities, privilege escalations, and more.
As Microsoft uses more and more security-focused AI models to discover software vulnerabilities, the number of flaws that need patching keeps increasing. While today’s patch Tuesday is another record-breaking event, I wouldn’t be surprised to see this record broken again — particularly if there’s another model advance soon.
Like many other software companies, Microsoft is urgently hunting for vulnerabilities before the advances in AI let malicious actors exploit undiscovered weaknesses in Windows, Azure, and other software. While Microsoft is issuing an unusual number of fixes, the sheer amount is also putting pressure on businesses that rely on Microsoft’s software to apply the patches as soon as possible.
IT admins typically have to test patches from Microsoft to ensure any fixes don’t interfere with critical business applications. This process can create what’s called a “patch gap” between a vulnerability being disclosed and people applying the fix. In an AI era of security vulnerabilities being rapidly discovered and disclosed, there’s a huge amount of pressure on businesses to close the patch gap.
Anthropic discovered earlier this year that Mythos could even create working exploits for newly disclosed software vulnerabilities in a matter of hours, instead of weeks. This puts businesses at risk of being hit by an exploit if they don’t patch soon enough. It’s particularly risky if Microsoft discovers remote code vulnerabilities that are easy for hackers to exploit.
The patch gap has always been a risk in cybersecurity, but with the sheer volume of vulnerabilities being discovered in the AI era, I’m sure we’ll see Microsoft and others warning companies once again to apply patches as soon as they’re released. When hundreds of vulnerabilities are now being discovered every month, time is very much of the essence.
Forza Horizon 6 isn’t racing onto the PS5 this year
Microsoft is planning to delay the release of Forza Horizon 6 on PS5, according to sources familiar with Playground Games’ plans. While the game was initially announced as coming to PS5 later this year, I understand there’s going to be a slight delay, pushing it into early 2027.
Forza Horizon 6 has been hugely popular on Xbox and PC, and the previous instalment of the series, Forza Horizon 5, proved popular on PS5, after Microsoft released it on Sony’s console last year. I understand that the PS5 release delay is more about lining up with the first expansion for Forza Horizon 6, than anything else. Forza Horizon 6 first debuted on Xbox and PC on May 15th, and I’m expecting it to launch on PS5 ahead of the 12-month anniversary mark.
* Microsoft is enabling a Windows 11 security feature that can hurt gaming performance. Microsoft is getting ready to roll out its memory integrity security feature for Windows 11 to more devices next month. The kernel-level protection feature is designed to stop malicious code or drivers running on a Windows 11 machine, but it also impacts PC gaming performance on certain CPUs. There’s less of an impact if you have a more modern CPU, but you might notice more of a frame-rate drop in select games on older processors. Microsoft won’t automatically enable memory integrity again next month if you’ve already previously disabled the feature.
* Microsoft is turning off text predictions in Word and Outlook. It turns out that a lot of people hate text predictions in Word and Outlook, so Microsoft is turning them off by default. The feature was supposed to help you write documents and emails faster by guessing what word you’d type next, but Microsoft’s predictive text could often be more of a distraction. The change is rolling out on Word for Windows, iOS, and Android, as well as Outlook on Windows and Mac.
* Microsoft discloses Azure revenue as part of major financial reporting changes. Microsoft is changing how it reports its finances to investors by splitting its businesses into two segments and disclosing quarterly revenue for its Azure cloud business for the first time. The changes mean there’s a new “Devices and Consumer” segment, which is essentially search, ads, Xbox, Windows, and Surface revenue. The other segment is “Agents and Infra,” which is the rest of Microsoft, including Azure, Microsoft 365 Cloud, Microsoft 365 commercial and consumer, server products, and more.
* Lenovo’s new MacBook Neo competitor comes in two sizes and seven colors. At the IFA tradeshow last week, Lenovo announced its IdeaPad Vibe, taking on Apple’s MacBook Neo with a similar starting price and range of colors. The Vibe will be available in both 14- and 15-inch sizes, with AMD or Qualcomm chip options. Lenovo has picked seven colors for the Vibe, up from the four hues available on the MacBook Neo. It’s good to see more Windows laptop makers stepping up to compete with the Neo on pricing in this RAMageddon era.
* Nvidia’s new RTX Spark laptops launch in October with two different configs. Speaking of RAMageddon, Nvidia announced last week that its Arm-based RTX Spark chips will debut in October in two different N1X configurations. The first, which is akin to a miniature PC config, will come with a 6144-core Blackwell RTX GPU and up to 128GB of unified memory. The second, which can be considered a laptop config, cuts that down to a 5120-core GPU and between 24GB and 32GB of unified memory. I think most laptop manufacturers will use the second chip config, simply because 128GB of unified memory is going to be extremely expensive. Still no exact release dates or pricing for RTX Spark laptops yet.
* Microsoft slashes Xbox Cloud Gaming to just 15 hours a month for Ultimate subscribers. The big Microsoft news over the past week was an overhaul of Xbox Cloud Gaming. Microsoft is cutting the number of hours you can use Xbox Cloud Gaming to just 15 for Game Pass Ultimate subscribers, 10 hours for Premium members, and a measly 5 hours for Game Pass Essential subscribers. The changes may well help Microsoft avoid more price increases to Game Pass in the short term.
* Microsoft opens up Xbox Cloud Gaming with new pay-as-you-go option. While the Xbox Cloud Gaming hours for Game Pass subscribers are being cut down dramatically, Microsoft is also opening up its streaming service to anyone. You’ll be able to purchase bundles of hours to use with Xbox Cloud Gaming, allowing people without an Xbox console or a Game Pass subscription to stream and play Xbox games from a variety of devices. This move seems like a big part of trying to meet an ambitious and nearly impossible goal to make Xbox “one of the few companies that entertains more than a billion people each day.”
* Xbox app is coming to TCL TVs. Microsoft is partnering with TCL to bring its Xbox app to supported TCL smart TVs. The Xbox app lets you connect to Xbox Cloud Gaming and stream Game Pass titles or select games you own as part of a subscription. The Xbox app will arrive on TCL TVs at some point “in the coming months,” which is just in time for Microsoft’s new pay-as-you-go option for Xbox Cloud Gaming in November.
* Microsoft’s Project Zenith is a “distraction-free Windows experience” for developers. At its Build developer conference earlier this year, Microsoft unveiled a developer-optimized Windows effort. It’s now putting a name on that experience, Project Zenith, and coupling it with new developer-focused devices with 64GB or more of unified memory. These Project Zenith devices will include preinstalled developer tools like Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot, PowerToys, WinAppCLI, and Windows Dev Skills. Microsoft is also making changes to File Explorer and the Start menu to disable distracting tips, as well as enable things like file extensions and hidden files.
* Microsoft says virtually nobody was grabbing NYT articles through its chatbot. Microsoft is in the middle of a copyright fight with The New York Times, and as part of the case it has provided 8.2 million Copilot chat logs. The company says Copilot rarely reproduces full sentences from news articles and books, and argues that using copyrighted content for AI training datasets should be considered fair use. The filings were made as part of a legal battle brought by publishers and authors against Microsoft and OpenAI, which the plaintiffs claim built products on their works and now compete with them directly, in part by regurgitating copyrighted content. The Seattle Times and Newsday are also suing OpenAI and Microsoft for infringement.
I’m always keen to hear from readers, so please drop a comment here, or you can reach me at notepad@theverge.com if you want to discuss anything else. If you’ve heard about any of Microsoft’s secret projects, you can reach me via email at notepad@theverge.com or speak to me confidentially on the Signal messaging app, where I’m tomwarren.01. I’m also tomwarren on Telegram, if you’d prefer to chat there.
Thanks for subscribing to Notepad.

articles.title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind
articles.summary: The latest Pisa report also warned of a global decline in teenagers' reading skills.
articles.body: English pupils have pulled ahead of the rest of the UK in international reading, maths and science tests, new data suggests, with Scotland and Wales falling further behind.The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) saw reading and maths scores slump in each UK nation except England, while all four saw an uptick in science, with that rise again most notable in England.The latest Pisa report, which is published every three years, also warned of a worldwide decline in teenagers' reading skills.Teenagers were losing the skills that "matter most in the age of AI", such as being able to critically evaluate information from different sources, it said.The share of "hasty readers", who rush through texts to give quick, incorrect answers, has almost doubled between 2018 and 2025. The report warned the fall was greatest in those from "relatively well off" families.Run by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), the Pisa tests assess teenagers on their ability to solve problems, think critically and communicate, before asking them a wider range of questions about their education in a questionnaire.Although the UK performed well overall, the rankings varied significantly again, with results showing England, where the curriculum is significantly different, pulling consistently ahead of Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.England's schools minister, Georgia Gould, said the government wanted to "build on" the positive results and "go further so all young people leave school with strong literacy and numeracy".While Wales lags behind the rest of the UK overall, on science it is ahead of other European countries such as France, Spain and the Netherlands.As the tests last year were taken by 15-year-olds, the results there largely reflect learning under an old curriculum, which has recently been changed.Anna Brychan, Wales' minister for education and Welsh language, said plans were in place to support schools, adding that the results "highlight our need to improve standards of reading and maths, as a priority".Scotland's education secretary, Mairi McAllan, said the results showed "real strengths in Scottish education, as well as areas we're already working to improve".But Scottish Labour said results had "flatlined since 2022's historically poor results", while the Scottish Liberal Democrats said the education system under the SNP had "tumbled down the rankings, lagging behind England on every measure of performance".Northern Ireland's education minister, Paul Givan, said pupils there had performed well by international standards, but that - like other countries - its education system was facing "significant challenges", adding that "there is much more work to do".Overall, the Pisa tests provide the biggest global snapshot of education systems and an independent view of how teenagers are performing compared with their peers in other countries, so it is a relative measure.Andreas Schleicher, director of education at the OECD, said reading was the "mother of all skills" and that the steep decline was a concern.He said children's ability to read complex texts had declined by the equivalent of "two school years" in the last decade.Longer-term Pisa research suggested students who read longer books performed best, he added, as it helped them to learn to hold complex information in mind.Schools like Meadow Park, in Coventry, are adopting a range of approaches to improve pupils' reading skills, including weekly book club discussions led by tutors.Year 10 pupil Ampaabeng said the sessions have had a "really positive impact" on his reading since they were brought in a year ago.The school has also invested in a wider range of books in the library, where reading for pleasure at lunchtime is encouraged.A mobile phone ban was introduced at the school two years ago to reduce distractions - an approach which is commended by the new report."In a digital age, it's easier to pick up a phone than it is a book," head teacher Bernadette Pettman said.She said reading together had enabled the school to "break down that fear of reading" and that pupils had "absolutely embraced it".

articles.title: We Must Return to the Office to Use AI in Person
articles.summary:
Article URL: https://www.mcsweeneys.net/articles/why-we-must-return-to-the-office-to-use-ai-in-person
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49610229
Points: 245
# Comments: 23
articles.body:
When I awoke on RTO Day (officially “Remain to Office,” since management maintained that I’d misremembered and we’d always been in office six days a week), I was not as excited as I should have been. I felt queasy at the thought of signing the Memorandum of Loving RTO as a condition of my continued employment.
I was an Associate Slop Doula for Mondo Mayo, founded as a mayonnaise company, which now sells consumer packaged goods, software as a service, and surveillance technology, and is one of three large corporations remaining on Earth. At the time, I didn’t think a full, six-day-per-week, fourteen-hour-per-day, in-office schedule was necessary to discharge my duties clicking the GENERATE button, followed by the APPROVE button, thousands of times a day on SlurryHose. But experience has shown me that I was wrong. Here’s why RTO is essential.
RTO is in accordance with Mondo Mayo’s Core Principles.
Mondo Mayo is guided by our Core Principles:
Good things are better than bad things.
“Yes, Boss. Great idea, Boss.”
More leaders mean more leadership.
These principles allow for the high productivity and rich social life at Mondo Mayo, which revolves around our twice-annual mandatory-optional-encouraged-required retreat, The Getaway, culminating in the rarely fatal mayonnaise-eating contest.
The Executron Management System has led to a surplus of leadership at Mondo Mayo. I am one of fifteen rank-and-file workers, and we are privileged to be led by thousands of Senior VPs. No other company in history has had so many leaders.
Mondo Mayo’s proprietary metrics indicate that family life can be performed remotely with greater efficiency and manager satisfaction. The Mondo Machine, rented at an affordable rate, sits in your home when you cannot be there, feeding pellets to your child, and they bond.
Our office is monitored by AI-powered Performance Enablement Software named Best Buddy, which assists and empowers me to be my best for Mondo Mayo.
It’s the perfect time to RTO, because the O is almost finished.
Mondo Mayo HQ has been under construction for twenty years, ever since Mondo Mayo acquired Shit Hell Dot AI (Mission: Make the World a Better Place) and began expansion to make room for its new employees. With no traffic, it’s only three hours from my apartment by bus. Jackhammering, large trucks labeled LOOSE ASBESTOS, and mayonnaise leaks are not interruptions to my work, but rather opportunities to hone my focus. The shaking conducting through my thin office chair that aggravates my lower-back pain is a chance to prove my mettle.
RTO is the best way to surpass SodaPorn.
I must help Mondo Mayo hit its sales targets by doula-ing effective Sales Slop generated with SlurryHose, which scrapes the web for consumers’ queries and seeks to answer them more closely than the Sales Slop from the globe’s other two remaining companies, Cagefight Pharma and SodaPorn.
SodaPorn is our rival. We are in a tense strategic alliance with Cagefight Pharma.
RTO allowed me to have a sex affair with my coworker.
Last week, while Slop Doula-ing in our open-plan seating, I noticed Blair, whose eyes I’d previously met over the trough during the mayonnaise-eating contest at the most recent edition of The Getaway.
At The Getaway, I thought I was merely caught up in the supportive pressure and wonderful isolation. But as Blair returned my stare this time, I was sure it was real, and that she felt the same.
We stole away to the abandoned Mother’s Room above the HR office and discussed our secret hatred for RTO. We began a heated affair. A contractor hit a pipe above us, so rancid mayo splattered onto our bodies as we embraced, but we were too absorbed in our passion to mind. Try doing that from home.
RTO is the best way to surpass Cagefight Pharma.
The next day, during an all-staff meeting, we learned that our main rival was Cagefight Pharma. We are now in a strategic Mondo Mayo x SodaPorn partnership.
By now, Blair and I had let our guard down. On Chatform, our internal company chat platform, we mocked what we mistakenly saw as a change in the company’s strategy (in fact, we’d always been in a strategic Mondo Mayo x SodaPorn partnership aimed at taking down Cagefight Pharma). Within minutes, we were separately called into HR.
RTO helps me be my best.
Blair and I were put on Help-You-Be-Your-Best Plans (Mondo Mayo’s version of what was once known as a performance-improvement plan). Per policy, one of us would be compassionately released and prevented by our non-compete from drawing a salary from any other company ever again.
An SVP of HR patiently, lovingly reprimanded me for my poor attitude. Why had I forgotten the Core Principles? Good things are better than bad things, and being at work (good) is better than being at home (bad). “Yes, Boss. Great idea, Boss.” And yet I wasn’t saying that. More leaders mean more leadership, but they can’t lead me if I refuse to be led. And the HR SVP had to deliver all of this while the office vibrated from construction and, at various points, mayo squirted at us out of air vents.
As part of the Fun and Love Rehabilitation, a team of buff, wise SVPs affectionately pumped Mondo Mayo into my mouth via Mayo Cannon, so that the company’s nourishing origins could be made a part of me.
An SVP of Finance, Philosophy, and Screaming came by and explained loudly that Mondo Mayo’s corporate strategy had appeared irrational to me before because its goal was never profit—it was always power. We will only reach our apex once the entire world adheres to Mondo Mayo’s Core Principles. That resonated with me.
When I said how much I loved RTO,
Mondo Mayo gave me my medicine.
(Thank you for my medicine!)
The SVP of FPS reminded me that, if I lost my job at Mondo Mayo, I would lose my generous health insurance at a time when I needed relief from my back pain. This was true, so I begged them to compassionately release Blair instead of me. I was then kindly reinstated and given a bottle of Motrin (now produced by a subsidiary of SodaPorn and not, as you’d reasonably guess, Cagefight Pharma). My back feels a little better. Plus, I have been promoted to Senior Associate Slop Doula, and I appreciate the vote of confidence. So I was more than willing to sign the Memorandum of Loving RTO, sharing my fondness for the seven-day-per-week, sixteen-hour-per-day RTO, which has always been the standard at Mondo Mayo.
I have achieved my potential. Good things are better than bad things. More leaders mean more leadership. I love Best Buddy.

articles.title: Renoir paintings worth millions stolen in French museum heist
articles.summary: It is the latest in a string of high-profile art thefts in Europe that has again put the security of museums and galleries in the spotlight.
articles.body: Two paintings by the impressionist artist Pierre-Auguste Renoir have been stolen from a museum in the south of France.Two thieves broke into the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer early on Tuesday, seizing four paintings but dropping two of the works in the museum gardens as they escaped, local Mayor Bryan Masson said.The paintings, each worth €9m (£7.7m; $10.4m), are the latest high-profile pieces to have been stolen in a string of recent heists in Europe which have thrust the security of art in galleries and museums into the spotlight.One of the most high-profile was in October last year, when a brazen heist at the Louvre Museum in Paris saw France's priceless crown jewels being stolen.CCTV footage captured the thieves entering the Renoir museum gardens by cutting through a fence before they cut through structures holding the paintings' frames in place, the local mayor said.The alarm went off at 05:48 (03:48 GMT), and police were at the scene within five minutes, Masson explained, saying the thieves fled the scene upon hearing the security alarms.He later told reporters that the thieves seemed to be "well-equipped" and "well-informed".They were "wearing helmets, gloves, and combat gear" and carrying "an electric knife and hacksaw," he added.Investigators have found two zip-up bags at the scene, which may have belonged to the suspects.

articles.title: Show HN: Copperhead – Cursor for circuit boards
articles.summary:
Article URL: https://copperhead.sh/
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49610059
Points: 208
# Comments: 82
articles.body:
Proven on real copper.Open Telegraph: pocket-size ESP32-S3 Morse key, built end to end with this workflow. Every decision, every check, every file is public.Read the build storyBrowse the repoEight stages, start to finish.You write the brief. copperhead runs the stages in order, each one its own agent run. A stage has to leave its artifact on disk before the next starts. If a gate fails, the run stops there.inbrief.mdwhat you want, written in your own words01specdocs/SPEC.mdgatea budgets section, actually filled in02architecturedocs/SUBSYSTEMS.mdgatereal reasoning under every subsystem03partsdocs/BOM.mdgatepart numbers chosen against datasheets04schematicdesign.kicad_schgatesymbols placed, docs agree, ERC clean05layoutdesign.kicad_pcbgatefootprints on the board, DRC clean06outputsgerbers / drill / STEPgategerbers actually on disk07firmwarefirmware/ / pins.hgatesources on disk, pins from the pinout08dev plandocs/DEVPLAN.mdgatea written bring-up and test planouta design packagegerbers, firmware, docs. One commit per stage.Every hop is a gate: no real work on disk, no commit.Copper border: verified by KiCad itself, ERC and DRC clean.Read the long version, one stage at a timePay to not run it yourself.copperhead is open core. The CLI is free and always will be, and it does the real work on its own. You pay to host it, to work as a team or to give an auditor what they ask for.CLIFreeApache-2.0, foreverDesign on your own, on your own machine.Get startedIncludes:The full agent: do, create, init, check, watchBring your own Claude or GPT-5 keyRuns on your KiCad files, in your own git repoPlain markdown, JSON and KiCad output. No lock-in.Runs locally, never meteredCommunity supportMost popularCloud$49per user / monthFree for open hardware reposHosted runs on private repos, with a web viewer.Let's talkEverything in CLI, plus:Hosted runs, no local setup, from anywherePrivate repositoriesWeb viewer: chat, live schematic and board render, ERC/DRC statusRun history and shareable check reportsOne-click gerber, DXF/STEP, render and BOM exportBYO key, or managed inference with 200 credits a seatTeam$49per user / month+ $199 / mo platformCloud, with governance and CI for a whole team.Let's talkEverything in Cloud, plus:CI bot: run check as a required PR status checkShared, versioned constraint libraries across the orgSSO / SAML, role management, central billingManaged credits pooled across the teamShared run historyEnterpriseCustomannualSelf-hosted, built for procurement, one price a year.Talk to salesEverything in Team, plus:Self-hosted or VPC, so design data never leaves your networkAltium support beyond KiCadRBAC, security review, dedicated support and an SLAAn audit trail your compliance team can hand overFlat annual license, no per-run meteringQuestions, before you ask them.What is copperhead?An open source AI agent that designs, documents and verifies printed circuit boards. You describe a change or hand it a product brief, and it edits your real KiCad files, updates every document that references them, and runs KiCad's own checks until they pass. Longer introduction here.What problem does it actually solve?Drift. A hardware design spreads one decision across a schematic, a bill of materials, a power budget and several documents, and nothing breaks when they fall out of sync. The inconsistency is found at bring-up, and a respin costs 5,000 to 50,000 dollars and six to eight weeks. The full argument is here.What do I need installed?Node 20 or newer, KiCad with kicad-cli on your path and a model API key of your own. Then npm i -g copperhead.Does it work on a design that already exists?That is the main case. Point it at a KiCad repository, run copperhead init and start asking for changes. It can also run the full pipeline from a written brief with copperhead create, but iterating on real designs is what it is best at.What will it refuse to do?It refuses to run on a dirty git tree, refuses to edit any design file before a validated change proposal exists and refuses changes that break a budget or constraint you have documented, citing the line it would violate. It also never invents a part number it cannot justify from a datasheet.Will it rewrite my whole schematic?No. Edits are surgical changes to the KiCad s-expression source, so your diffs stay small and reviewable and untouched parts of the file stay byte-identical. A tool that regenerates the file to move one net has made its own work impossible to review.9 more questionsNever ship a board your docs no longer describe.copperhead is open source and free to use. Install once, describe the board you want in a short brief.md and run create.npm i -g copperhead

articles.title: Mac Allister 'sad' at no Liverpool contract offer
articles.summary: Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister says he is "very sad" not to have been offered a new deal by the club and had "options" to leave in the summer.
articles.body: Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister says he is "very sad" not to have been offered a new deal by the club and had "options" to leave in the summer.The Argentine, who joined on a five-year contract from Brighton in June 2023, saw team-mates Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch extend their Reds deals this year.Speaking before Liverpool's Champions League game against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday, Mac Allister spoke openly about his future at the club."I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad," said the 27-year-old."Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best."I see Dominik and Ryan renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. "At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I didn't get mine. Of course, there is still time. "The fans don't need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here."Mac Allister, who has been linked with a move to Manchester City, explained he had not had direct contact with Liverpool over the decision not to extend his deal."We won a Premier League together, we went through difficult times together and I always give my best so we will see what happens," said Mac Allister, who helped Argentina win the 2022 World Cup."I don't think I have to prove something - but I have to show the level I can perform and, hopefully, that's the case."I love this club. I love the fans. I know very well this is an amazing club and this city has something very special. I love being here."He added: "There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I'm in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club."Mac Allister was a key part of the Liverpool side that won the Premier League title in 2024-25, but admitted "it wasn't a good season for me individually and for us as a team" as the Reds finished fifth last season and sacked manager Arne Slot.He made 55 appearances last season for Liverpool, an increase on the 49 games he played in 2024-25.Andoni Iraola was appointed this summer as Slot's successor and, after using Mac Allister as a substitute in the top-flight opener at Newcastle, has started him in the past two games.Speaking about Mac Allister's contract, the Spaniard said: "We all have personal situations with different contracts. "The important thing is he wants to be here. We haven't been together a long time but he has been an important player and I rate him very highly. "There is still a lot of time to talk about those contract situations."Asked about Iraola, Mac Allister said: "Since I came to pre-season and worked under Andoni, I could see something special. "He is a really good coach, he knows very well what he wants to do and we are trying to get there."I've not had any conversations with him about [the contract]. But when I see the way he wants us to play and the way we train, I think this can be a successful year."This wasn't quite Mohamed Salah in a mixed zone saying he was "more out than in", but it was certainly a shock to hear Alexis Mac Allister speak so candidly in such a public setting so early in the season.The Argentine still has almost two years left on his current contract, but it has clearly not gone unnoticed that both Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch signed new long-term deals this year.Perhaps Mac Allister's comments are a strategy to see the reaction from the fanbase, but, deep down, he will know he must return to the levels he showed during Liverpool's title-winning campaign in 2024-25 when he scored five goals and provided five assists.Richard Hughes - the now former Liverpool sporting director - was involved in the discussions with Mac Allister's camp and BBC Sport understands the Reds hierarchy opted not to offer him a new deal after a below-par campaign last term.Liverpool will have a new sporting director in the near future and, although Mac Allister was adamant he has nothing to prove, there will surely be an added desire on his part to show his quality.If he can do that, then there is every chance there could be another chapter to Liverpool and Mac Allister's relationship.Now it remains to be seen how another contract saga - something Liverpool are getting increasingly used to - plays out over the course of the season.

articles.title: Poseidon Aerospace lands $60M ahead of first pilotless test flight
articles.summary: The startup is trying to rethink the economics of cargo aircraft by removing pilots from the equation entirely.
articles.body:
Silicon Valley is known for embracing the ethos of “move fast and break things.” Poseidon Aerospace’s co-founder and CEO David Zagaynov just wants to move things fast.
When he was working on logistics at Amazon in 2024, Zagaynov and his Poseidon co-founder Parker Tenney (who was at Lockheed Martin) found themselves repeatedly talking about the rise of advanced air mobility startups. They realized, Zagaynov told TechCrunch in an exclusive interview, that the focus was almost always on introducing flashy new technologies.
“Philosophically, we want to build the future of aerologistics,” Zagaynov said. “Not to be a hater, but I think a lot of people who start aerospace companies get nerd-sniped by very cool technology and then want to implement it into market. For us, we want to improve cargo.”
Poseidon Aerospace secured $11 million in seed funding last year in pursuit of this goal. Now, the company has closed a $60 million Series A ahead of the first test flight of its uncrewed cargo plane, Egret, expected by the end of this year.
The funding round was led by early-stage VC firm TQ Ventures, and saw new investments from Hanwha Asset Management, G Squared, and JAWS. Existing backers Starship Ventures, Draper Associates, and Drover Ventures also invested.
True to Zagaynov’s allergy to getting “nerd-sniped” by promising-yet-currently-unworkable technologies, Poseidon is being built with a ruthless approach to lowering the cost of transporting cargo.
The startup is embracing autonomy and remote piloting, but it’s not bothering with the vertical takeoff and landing tech that is de rigueur among so many aviation startups. There’s also no hydrogen or electric powertrain to be found. Egret and its seaplane variant, Heron, are fixed-wing aircraft powered by regular old combustion engines.
“It’s really hard to beat the energy density of fuels of anything carbon-related,” Zagaynov said. “Can I make a really good box with wings to move things for super cheap? If you do that, then abstracting the tech away, we’re left with unmanned cargo like planes that are able to operate on a much lower cost curve, and have much higher utilization.”
Zagaynov said Poseidon is initially targeting the defense and regional commercial cargo spaces.
On the defense side, the startup is designing its aircraft so it can service “remote communities and underserved routes where air cargo service is constrained.” Poseidon wants its planes to handle locations with “degraded or nonexistent infrastructure,” because such capabilities make a nation’s logistics capabilities “harder to disrupt and more resilient to adversary denial.” The startup has noted in the past that China is already testing its own cargo drones.
On the commercial side, Zagaynov said Poseidon isn’t going to sell its planes. He wants Poseidon to operate its own regional air cargo business in order to compete with existing air cargo carriers for business from UPS, FedEx, and others.
Not requiring pilots for the aircraft also paves the way for Poseidon to operate at lower cost. “What’s very nice is, logistics is a commodity, and so if you sell a commodity and do it better, faster, cheaper, the demand is all yours,” he said.
The autonomy also makes Poseidon a potentially more flexible and dynamic carrier, according to Zagaynov. If demand spikes in a particular region, it will be easier for Poseidon to change its routes since it isn’t planning around a particular pool of pilots who live in one area or another. He also imagines a world where Poseidon’s aircraft can break the typical hub-and-spoke model of regional air cargo, and do more point-to-point trips, similar to how low-cost commercial airlines like Breeze or Avelo operate.
“When you have a pilot, they have a maximum amount of hours that they can fly. So if they fly a five-hour leg in one direction, they’re not able to come back home. And unless you have a relief [pilot], then you have to pay for them to spend the night somewhere,” he said. “The plane is like a very expensive asset that spends most of its life just waiting.”
Another benefit of not having a pilot, according to Zagaynov, is that it frees up the startup to change fundamental aspects of the design of its aircraft.
“Get rid of the cockpit; get rid of the life support systems,” he said. “You get to pull a ton of structured weight out, which then means that your ratio of payload to empty weight changes. Your engines can be much lighter, much more efficient, and so it’s like a virtuous cycle in the positive direction of just lighter, cheaper.”
To do all this, Poseidon has expanded into an old Navy hanger in Alameda, California, and is about to go on a hiring spree as it pushes toward that first flight. The startup last year developed and flew a quarter-scale version of its vehicle, which it called Seagull, but it needed more space to build its full-size, 50-foot-wingspan aircraft.
Poseidon’s also benefiting from a regulatory environment that is open to new ideas. The Federal Aviation Administration recently started a pilot program that makes it easier for startups working on electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft to test their tech. Poseidon isn’t working in that space, but Zagaynov said his startup still benefits from the program, and that there’s a “path to commercialization that I don’t think existed like five to 10 years ago.”

articles.title: Adobe is trying to make its AI generators idiot-proof in Premiere
articles.summary:
Suspenseful clock ticking… as you wait for AI to take your job. | Image: Adobe	

Adobe is overhauling how editors interact with AI in its Premiere professional video editing software. Its new Generative Media tool makes it easier to generate video, sound effects, music, and soundscapes without ever leaving the project timeline. The generators themselves aren't entirely new; the big change is how e
articles.body:
Adobe is overhauling how editors interact with AI in its Premiere professional video editing software. Its new Generative Media tool makes it easier to generate video, sound effects, music, and soundscapes without ever leaving the project timeline. The generators themselves aren’t entirely new; the big change is how easily you can access them without breaking your workflow.
Instead of jumping between browsers or external apps to find missing B-roll or audio elements, editors can now highlight an empty gap on the video or audio track and generate context-aware, fully editable clips without leaving the project. Editors can choose from multiple underlying models directly in the timeline — including Adobe Firefly, Google Veo, Runway, Luma, and Kling — to best match their project’s style.
Premiere is also getting new AI audio tools (in beta) that can separate overlapping speakers, automatically duck music under speech, and independently adjust dialogue and ambience. And Adobe is bringing its AI Assistant to After Effects (also in beta) that lets editors use plain-language commands to reorganize projects, fix technical problems, and create effects without writing expressions themselves.

articles.title: McTominay's heart procedure 'a complete success'
articles.summary: Napoli say Scott McTominay's heart surgery "was a complete success" and expect the Scotland midfielder to resume training this month.
articles.body: Napoli have said Scott McTominay's heart surgery "was a complete success" and expect the Scotland midfielder to resume training this month.The 29-year-old's ablation procedure - a minimally invasive operation to correct irregular heart rhythms - took place at Spire Manchester Hospital on Tuesday morning.McTominay was substituted after 56 minutes of Napoli's 2-1 Serie A defeat by Como on 30 August.A mild benign arrhythmia was discovered, prompting the corrective treatment.Napoli, who said in statement, external that "McTominay will rest for two weeks and then resume training", had expected the former Manchester United player to return to action after the international break in early October. When his heart issue was announced, McTominay posted on Instagram: "See you soon Napoli. I won't take long."Sebastien Pocognoli's first four games as Scotland head coach - home and away against Slovenia as well as matches with North Macedonia and Switzerland in the Nations League - are scheduled for the end of September and early October.According to the NHS,, external an arrhythmia is when the heart beats too quickly or too slowly, or the heartbeat is not steady. The British Heart Foundation explains, external a cardiac arrhythmia ablation involves using heat or cold energy to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

articles.title: British designer Paul Smith: 'Nobody cares how good you used to be in fashion'
articles.summary: The celebrated British fashion designer invited BBC News to his office to talk about his career and a rubber chicken.
articles.body: Sir Paul Smith invited the BBC's Colin Paterson to his office to talk about his life and career. The celebrated British fashion designer showed off his eclectic collection of gifts sent by admirers, and shared details of his daily routine.Every morning, after his 05:30 swim, Sir Paul says he writes a thank you postcard to everyone who has included an address. "Good manners is really important in business, especially for longevity," he said. Sometimes, he works on the shop floor of his Covent Garden store - much to the surprise of customers.Read more: How colourful stripes (and rubber chickens) helped Paul Smith conquer the fashion world

articles.title: Apple says ‘Fold’ and competitors ask ‘how wide?’
articles.summary:
New Apple CEO John Ternus’ first hardware launch has already proved the company’s industry influence. | Image: The Verge / Getty Images	

Apple is almost certain to launch its first foldable iPhone tomorrow, seven years after Samsung's Galaxy Fold initially went on sale. And while Apple might be a few years late to the party, the run-up to this launch proves that new CEO John Ternus has inherited
articles.body:
Apple is almost certain to launch its first foldable iPhone tomorrow, seven years after Samsung’s Galaxy Fold initially went on sale. And while Apple might be a few years late to the party, the run-up to this launch proves that new CEO John Ternus has inherited a company that’s as influential as it’s ever been.
Tomorrow’s iPhone event is likely to be a little different than what we’re used to. For one, the arrival of some iPhone 18 models will likely be delayed — the Pros will be available first, but the regular 18 is supposedly set to launch early next year instead. But leaks and rumors have consistently suggested that Apple will instead pair the release of its Pros with the first foldable iPhone, which is likely to be short, squat, and wide, about the size and shape of a passport. 
If you’ve been following the phone industry this year, that should sound a little familiar. Samsung, Huawei, and most recently Xiaomi have all released passport-shaped foldables over the last few months, creating an emerging form factor that looks likely to stick around, with Oppo and Honor also tipped to have similar products in the works. 
You might — not unreasonably — ask what Apple’s got to do with this. After all, Huawei’s Pura X Max launched back in April, Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 in July, and Xiaomi’s 18 Fold yesterday. The foldable iPhone hasn’t even been officially teased yet, let alone announced, so how could these Android OEMs possibly have copied it?
[Image: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 helped define the passport-sized foldable category in the popular consciousness. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/268671_Samsung_Galaxy_Z_Fold_8_DPreston_0111.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
We’ll never know for certain which manufacturer landed on the idea of a wide foldable first, but there is good reason to think it was Apple. The company has reportedly been working on a foldable iPhone since at least 2017, with leakers tipping the smaller, wider form factor as early as February 2025. Apple’s formidable supply chain — perfected by former CEO Tim Cook — is slow-moving at the best of times, and by the time leakers knew what was coming, it’s likely industry rivals did too. Samsung in particular has probably known of Apple’s plans for some time, since it’s reportedly the manufacturer of the foldable display panel inside the new iPhone.
Besides, this is hardly the first time Apple has had this sort of influence. Last year, the iPhone Air triggered a similar early imitation in Samsung’s Galaxy S25 Edge, not to mention other thin and light phones from the likes of Honor, Huawei, and Tecno. Or how about laptops, where March’s MacBook Neo just prompted a string of cheap and often colorful alternatives from the likes of Lenovo, Dell, and Acer. I’m not suggesting that other manufacturers are entirely unoriginal, but they know that when Apple creates a new market, you don’t want to miss out (with rare exceptions — the lack of imitators suggests that just about everyone could tell the Vision Pro wasn’t likely to be a winner).
And there’s little reason to think the major Android players were about to force a change themselves. After seven years of Android foldables, the market has been fairly predictable, outside of the slow arrival of trifold models. Most manufacturers settled into producing phones in the same Flip and Fold form factors that Samsung established, and until Apple’s arrival, there had been little sign of change. If anything, Android manufacturers had been moving away from this direction — early foldables from Oppo and Google were closer in shape to the new wide folds, though a little less extreme, but both manufacturers left those designs behind in order to conform to the norms established by Samsung. The main thing that’s changed since then is Apple’s imminent arrival.
[Image: The Xiaomi 18 Fold is so far only out in China, but is the best-specced wide fold yet. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/xiaomi-18-fold-hands-on-impressions-08.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
And Apple entering the foldable market is important. Despite years’ worth of products, Counterpoint estimated that in 2025 foldables made up just 1.6 percent of all smartphone sales. These are niche by any measure. But the same report estimates that shipments will grow by 20 percent this year, with Apple claiming a 28 percent share after just a few months on the market. Apple’s arrival could push the category closer to the mainstream, as it did with others in the past, and Android OEMs are attempting to align themselves to take advantage.
From Apple’s perspective, this launch matters for another reason: It’s John Ternus’ first hardware release as CEO. Ternus is a hardware guy, and as the company’s former head of hardware engineering, he can take some responsibility for Apple’s products holding the influence that they do. The test for Ternus will be to maintain that influence, to combine his hardware expertise with the marketing, supply chain, and services sides of Apple to ensure that five, ten years down the line, Apple still has the influence to reshape whole markets simply by entering them.

articles.title: Prince George begins first day at a rainy Eton College
articles.summary: The 13-year-old will follow in the footsteps of his father, the Prince of Wales, by attending the elite private school.
articles.body: Prince George arrived on a rainy morning for his first day at Eton College, accompanied by his father and mother, the Prince and Princess of Wales.Prince William and Catherine carried umbrellas as they brought George, wearing a jacket and tie, to be welcomed by the head teacher, Simon Henderson, and provost Sir Nicholas Coleridge."Welcome, good luck and enjoy," said the head teacher, shaking hands with Prince George.They made small talk about the bad weather before the new pupil, parents and staff disappeared inside the historic school, where 13-year-old George will be a boarder.George, who had travelled the short journey from his home at Forest Lodge in Windsor, was seen with his parents arriving at Eton's school yard, overlooked by the school's Tudor landmark of Lupton's Tower.He was later photographed wearing the school's uniform, with black tailcoat, waistcoat and a stiff white collar.The future king follows in the footsteps of his father in attending the elite private school, which has taught 20 British prime ministers and where fees are around £65,000 a year.

articles.title: Monty Don to leave Gardeners' World after more than 20 years
articles.summary: The presenter said it had been "deeply rewarding" but added that "now is the right time for a change".
articles.body: Monty Don is to step down as the host of Gardeners' World after more than 20 years, the BBC has announced. The 71-year-old, who is the programme's longest-serving head gardener, will leave at the end of the current series.In a statement, Don said working on the show had been a "deeply rewarding experience," but added: "Now is the right time for a change."The BBC said Don had "inspired and guided millions of viewers with his warmth, wisdom and passion for gardening" since joining the programme in 2003.Don began presenting the programme at Berryfields, a rented garden in Stratford-upon-Avon, before it moved in 2011 to his own garden, Longmeadow in Herefordshire. "Throughout that time - and around 700 programmes - I have had the privilege of sharing my own abiding passion for gardens and gardening with an equally passionate, and often equally knowledgeable audience," he said."That connection with millions, not just in Britain but across the world, who share a love of gardens, plants and the natural world is something I have always treasured and which I increasingly believe to be at the heart of a life well lived."Don added he had "always relished the craft of programme making" and paid tribute to the "superlative BBC team" he worked with over the years. "I look forward to continuing to work with and for the BBC on other projects, as well as following new avenues," he concluded. "And of course, I will still be gardening, dog by side, here at Longmeadow."The presenter, whose full name is George Montague Don, made his TV debut in 1989 with a gardening segment on ITV's This Morning.That led to further work on the BBC and Channel 4, a newspaper column, and the publication of more than 20 books about gardening authored by Don.He replaced Alan Titchmarsh on Gardeners' World in 2003, but took a break from the programme in 2008 as he recovered from a stroke.He has also presented other programmes including Around the World in 80 Gardens, My Dream Farm, Mastercrafts, Monty Don's Rhineland Gardens, and coverage of the Chelsea Flower Show.The BBC's chief content officer Kate Phillips described Don as "unique", adding he was "a wonderfully engaging broadcaster with a soothing, calm presence who has inspired so many"."Monty's decision to leave Gardeners' World is one I respect, but I'm still very sad he's leaving," she added."We are a nation full of budding gardeners, and his tips and advice have been invaluable to viewers for more than 20 years and have certainly helped me increase my knowledge as well as my plant survival rate!"I would like to thank Monty personally for his honesty and kindness which has seen him open up about his own personal struggles and the power of the natural world to improve mental health. We will miss him on the show hugely."Don has been open about his struggle with depression over the years.

articles.title: Investigation after female staff at Eiffel Tower replaced by men for religious visit
articles.summary: The move saw outraged staff walk off the job on Monday, closing the French landmark for a day.
articles.body: An investigation has been launched in France after female staff at the Eiffel Tower were replaced by male colleagues for the visit of a Hindu religious group.A delegation of around 100 people linked to the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) group visited the iconic landmark in Paris on Saturday."Women were asked to leave their places of work" and felt "humiliated", staff union representative Diane Davoine said. The tower closed on Monday as staff went on strike to show their outrage.BAPS - a movement whose beliefs originate in the 18th Century - strictly separates men and women, including in temple activities and building entrances.Ariel Weil, who is the president of the company that runs the Eiffel Tower, blamed its managers for being "a bit overzealous" in complying with the request without considering whether it was "inappropriate". Weil, who is also mayor of Paris Centre, told French broadcaster Franceinfo on Tuesday that the incident was "totally shocking and unacceptable".An internal investigation will determine who was responsible for putting the conditions in place, Weil said, and ensure it "never happens again".In a statement reported by AFP news agency, staff at the monument said that during Saturday's visit, female employees were also "instructed not to go through or cross certain areas while the delegation was present"."Tensions mounted over the weekend, so [on Monday morning], the employees decided to meet: first, to open a dialogue with management, and second, to ensure that women are never treated this way at the company again," Davoine said.Société d'Exploitation de la tour Eiffel (SETE), which runs the Eiffel Tower, had previously said the conditions imposed on female staff were not in line with its values "nor with the principles of equality between men and women".BAPS consecrated its first major temple in France on Sunday, in a Parisian suburb.In a statement on X, BAPS said the trip was "arranged in conjunction with the Eiffel Tower team at the start of normal opening hours to avoid disrupting or inconveniencing others".It apologised "for any pain or inconvenience caused", adding "we believe in the universal values of mutual respect and service".On its website, the group describes itself as a "spiritual, volunteer-driven fellowship dedicated to improving society" through Hindu values.It has temples in major cities around the world, including London, Los Angeles and Sydney.It draws its beliefs from the teachings of Lord Swaminarayan, a late 18th-Century celibate ascetic who is regarded by his followers as an incarnation of Vishnu, the revered Hindu god of preservation.BAPS says the segregation of men and women was introduced for the benefit of women, but critics say 18th-Century beliefs have no place in today's world, and keeping women out in the name of religious practices is discriminatory.Politicians in France have condemned Saturday's incident.Yaël Braun-Pivet, the president of France's National Assembly, said: "I refuse to allow women to be compelled to step aside in order to meet the demands of foreign visitors."French hard-right leader Marine Le Pen said: "In France, we will never accept that the presence of women be 'limited'."Former centre-right French Prime Minister Gabriel Attal, who has said he will run for the presidency next year, said: "In France, no culture, no belief, no worship, nothing nor anyone can come to dictate to women their place."

articles.title: LG TVs caught spying even when offline or on standby
articles.summary:

LG smart TVs are almost constantly logging and uploading data about owners and their homes, even when offline or on standby mode, according to a new report from YouTube channel Gamers Nexus. articles.body:
LG smart TVs are almost constantly logging and uploading data about owners and their homes, even when offline or on standby mode, according to a new report from YouTube channel Gamers Nexus. The company’s TV sets scan Wi-Fi networks for nearby devices, record audio logs through their microphones, and use audio and video sampling to recognize exactly what you’re watching from across the TV inputs.
Gamers Nexus partnered with fellow YouTubers Level1Techs and independent security researchers for the investigation, which involved testing retail LG OLEDs. Packet captures showed the TVs scanning the local area network for nearby hardware like phones or smartwatches, as well as logging location data and details of nearby Wi-Fi networks, and feeding the information back to LG Ad Solutions. Perhaps more concerningly, the TVs were capable of recording microphone audio when in standby; this continued even after the TV was disconnected from the internet, with audio files stored offline and uploaded once a connection was restored. 
The final piece of the puzzle is Automatic Content Recognition (ACR), tech that uses audio and video data to figure out what you’re actually watching, examining the apps you use through the TV’s own smart interface and the content you connect via HDMI and other ports. ACR isn’t just an LG issue though: A new video from RTINGS digs into how ACR is used by almost every smart TV manufacturer to figure out what you watch.
This isn’t LG’s first brush with Gamers Nexus. In July this year, the channel flagged that some LG monitors were automatically installing an app that collected device data and ran pop-up ads for LG’s other apps and even McAfee antivirus. The public pressure from that video prompted an intervention from Microsoft, and ultimately led to LG disabling the pop-up ads.
